earlier_scan.source_named: Helbig, Karl 1933-34. Die Lubu-Sprache auf Sumatra; also Butar-Butar et al. 1984. Morfologi dan Sintaksis Bahasa Siladang. Neither reachable online (kemdikbud repository down).

sources.citation: Butar-Butar, Maruli; Abu Bakar; Urich Hamonangan Damanik. 1984. Morfologi dan Sintaksis Bahasa Siladang. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xiii+131 pp. (CORE mirror of repositori.kemdikbud,https://core.ac.uk/download/227144369.pdf)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Brief phoneme inventory only (pp. 7-8: 7 vowels, 19 consonants, after Simorangkir 1979:16). Scope statement p. 2: 'Patut dijelaskan bahwa hal yang diteliti pada kesempatan ini adalah data bahasa yang bersifat segmental saja. Data kebahasaan yang bersifat suprasegmental diharapkan dapat diteliti pada kesempatan yang akan datang.' Repeated p. 126 ('hal-hal yang bersifat suprasegmental masih belum termasuk dalam penelitian ini').

sources.note: Silent. Only remarks that speakers 'speak quickly and use vowels ɔ, ə, aə' and have /v/. Literature review names Manurung et al. 1978 (phonology & morphology), Butar-Butar 1984, Pawiro & Siwi 2005, and Syarfina & Sinar 2010 'Prosodi Bahasa Siladang Sumatera Utara' (USU) which 'illustrated the prosody and recorded 26 phonemes'.

sources.citation: Tengku Syarfina. 2009. Suprasegmental Bahasa Siladang. BAHAS (FBS Universitas Negeri Medan) No. 75 Th. XXXVI. DOI 10.24114/bhs.v0i75TH XXXVI.2539 (PDF viahttps://www.neliti.com/publications/79500/download;publisher galley 404)
sources.note: Experimental-phonetic (IPO-style) study of F0, intensity and per-syllable vowel duration in one declarative, one interrogative and one imperative sentence, male vs female speakers; gives phoneme list (7 V, 19 C, diphthongs ai/au, from Manurung 1978:5-6). No statement about the position of word stress/accent.

sources.citation: Moh. Masrukhi. 2002. Refleksi Fonologis Protobahasa Austronesia (PAN) pada Bahasa Lubu (BL). Humaniora 14(1): 86-93. DOI 10.22146/jh.v14i1.749
sources.note: Historical phonology of Lubu consonants using Helbig's Die Lubu-Sprache auf Sumatra wordlist as data (cites Helbig p. 16: 19 consonants; author counts 20). Segmental only; silent on stress.
